method.canonicalisation: Provider records are grouped into one disaster when they share a hazard family and fall inside that hazard’s matching window. Where either record is placed at an area centre, kilometres between them say nothing, so the match is by country and time instead.
method.significance: An event enters this ledger when deaths or missing are reported, at least 1,000 people are displaced, at least 10,000 affected, an authority raised a red or orange alert, ReliefWeb declared a disaster, or an earthquake reached magnitude 6. Each row states which of those applied.
method.sightings: Each event records the runs during which it was actually being carried by a provider, not only the last time it was seen. A single latest timestamp is overwritten on the next run, which destroys the evidence that a disaster was in the feed throughout a forecast window that has since closed. Consecutive sightings more than 6 hours apart start a new run rather than being joined.
method.frozen: A recorded event’s identity - canonical id, hazard, onset and the geography it was first seen at - is never rewritten. Impact figures are, because they are still being learned, and every change is appended to that event’s revisions. A revision marked administrative is bookkeeping rather than an observation: a figure carried across when two rows turned out to be one disaster, stamped with the merge time and not with any reading. Nothing reads it as impact that occurred.
method.retainedSnapshots: A verified fallback record held in the application is served only when the live providers do not carry the event, so it is evidence that the disaster happened and not evidence of when it was last seen. A row backed on a run by nothing but such records gains no sighting for that run and keeps whatever sighting history it already had; a row that has never been carried live says so, under retainedSnapshotOnly. Counted each run under lastRun.sightingsWithheldFromRetainedSnapshots.
method.supporting: Observations below the bar are not disasters and are not recorded as any, but a frozen conditional claim - an aftershock outlook - is graded on “observed aftershock activity”, which is mostly made of events that hurt nobody. Where such a claim accepts the hazard, the observation falls inside its window, and it falls inside the geography that claim named, the observation is kept under supporting, apart from the disasters. Each says which claim keeps it and which disaster that claim follows, because hazard, window and distance alone cannot tell two neighbouring sequences apart - two aftershock outlooks for mainshocks 150 km apart accept each other’s aftershocks in full. An observation that more than one sequence claims is graded for neither. They enter no recall figure and are never counted as disasters; where no conditional claim needs one, nothing is kept.
method.identity: A canonical id is a country, a rounded position and a minute, so two separate disasters can derive the same one. An id already held is believed only where the provider records overlap or the two rows can be the same occurrence under this hazard’s matching window; otherwise the new disaster is recorded under a distinguished id, carrying the id it derived and the measured reason the two were not merged.
method.notCounted: Hazard records below the bar above are real and are not disasters anyone failed to predict; they are left out of the recall denominator rather than deleted from the feed. The bar decides what enters: a disaster already recorded goes on being reconciled on every run even when it eases below it, because what is still being learned about it - how long it was carried, when it ended, what it did - does not stop being true. Each row keeps the reason it qualified on entry, under significanceAtEntry, beside the current assessment.
method.observationsOnly: Only a record whose evidence state is an observation is eligible. A forecast is not one, and neither is an official warning: a warning says severe weather is expected, and recording one as a disaster that happened would inflate the recall denominator and manufacture false negatives against forecasts that had nothing to miss. Each run states how many records it set aside on that ground, under lastRun.providerRecordsNotObservations.
